gallery.title: File:Absalom-Jones Peale.jpg
gallery.description: Raphaelle Peale was the first son of the American painter Charles Willson Peale and one of a large number of artist-children born to that branch of the Peale family. While Raphaelle was perhaps most famous for his still-life paintings, his portraits are highly regarded. The Reverend Absalom Jones was the prominent black minister of the St. Thomas African Episcopal Church in Philadelphia. Born a slave in Sussex, Delaware, Jones eventually won his freedom, was a founding member of the Free African Society, was ordained the first black priest of the Episcopal denomination, and helped to organize a school for black children.

gallery.description:
Cartoon drawing of a man with black hair wearing a black overcoat and holding a black bible.
Absalom Jones was a pioneering figure in the fight for social justice and equality. Formally enslaved, Jones became one of the first ordained Black ministers in the United States and helped found, with Richard Allen, the Free African Society. He was instrumental in helping the sick and afflicted during the Yellow Fever epidemic in Philadelphia.
